title: 11th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:00 with 32 members present. The first item was an urgent question under Rule 192 from the Vaikaradhoo member about big yellowfin tuna (bodukanneli) fishers who could not sell over 120 tonnes of catch; the House voted 40-0 to debate it. Members from both sides argued over who was responsible for the fishers' problems and what the government had promised on prices and factories, and the one-hour debate limit ran out with no further decision. The House then resumed the debate on the government's bill amending the Judges Act (Law 13/2010), but time ran out with no vote; the next sitting was set for 7 July 2025 at 09:00.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 32 present, 6 on leave, 5 on official travel

items.title: Urgent question (Rule 192) on big yellowfin tuna fishers unable to sell their catch
items.outcome: House voted 40-0 to debate it; one-hour debate held, time expired

items.title: Unfinished business: continuing debate on the Bill to amend the Judges Act (Law 13/2010), submitted by the government
items.outcome: debated; not concluded, to continue at the next sitting

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the urgent question was properly accepted by the House and that raising such issues is the House's duty to hold the government accountable.
Raised a point of order concerning remarks made about members.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Presented the urgent question: over 120 tonnes of big yellowfin unsold; asked the government to act on its promised buying price and fisher share.
Said he raised it to draw government attention and urged action on the pledges made to fishers.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Thanked members for accepting the urgent question; said unsold catch and falling prices worry fishers and promised factory and prices have not materialised.
Said the Judges Act amendments would bring judges under government control and that justice delays have other causes.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said delays in tuna sales are a genuine concern but that the previous government left the sector weakened and factories idle.
Said fishers are now paid within 48 hours and that policies take time.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Said fishers' complaint is about getting a fair price for their catch, and that this is not a new problem.
Called on the government to fulfil its promises to fishers.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said the fishing industry is important but the government inherited heavy debts that limit investment in factories.
Spoke on the Judges Act bill about delays in justice, court backlogs and the need for judges to meet conduct standards.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said earlier governments did not resolve fishers' problems, while the current government settles payments within 24 hours; welcomed the issue being raised.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Argued the urgent question was not political, and that the earlier government's record on fishing was poor while the current one is working on promises.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the question did not meet Rule 192's urgency condition, and that the problem will be resolved under the current government.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said fishers' rights were secured under the current government, which pays within 48 hours and arranged access to loans.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the unsold catch is a real problem affecting many fishers, and urged the government to find solutions rather than deny it.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the question was brought because of unsold fish at Hulhumale, citing the pledged cooperative, the price floor and a drop in tuna exports.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said the government is building new factories and paying fishers within 48 hours, and defended its record on the sector.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said past governments weakened the fishing industry, and that the current government pays fishers within 48 hours and is clearing the backlog.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order that another member was making false statements in the chamber.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said the Judges Act amendments aim to strengthen judges' independence and that past judicial appointments were politically influenced.

decisions: The House voted 40-0 to take up and debate the urgent question on tuna fishers.
Debate on the Judges Act amendment bill was not concluded and will continue at the next sitting on 7 July 2025 at 09:00.
